chapter: Rising in Manhattan: clubs, Hilda and the Latin scene
title: Mario and Machito as their own promoters
summary: They booked their own dances, advertised on radio, and drew on the Puerto Rican colony of El Barrio.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Okay. Are you saying now that you and Mario were the booking agents for your own band?
Is that the only way you got that job, or did you want to do it?
No, that's the only way we got that job because we don't know nobody.
In other words, you had to sell so many tickets or, or .........

I went to the WBNX in that particular time - that it was one hour from six to seven, remember? Oh! you was a baby then, and I put an announcement: 'The Best Orchestra in the World', you know, meaning like my grandmother would talk.
You had a radio show, was it at that time or did it come later?
Okay, all right. You got the job at the Park Plaza so, ah Montecino was out and you was in.
Okay. How long did you work at the Park Plaza?
So you and Mario were your own promotors of the band?
Yes,...and we got all the dances because our telephone was well-known for practically everyone and you know, the colony was about thirty-five thousand - forty-thousand.......
